description: A two-panel age-hardening figure. Both panels are scatter plots with error bars of "Hardness, BHN" (y-axis, 200-400, major ticks every 50) versus "Time in Hours" on a logarithmic x-axis (0.1-1000 h); the caption identifies the aging temperature as 530 °C. (a) is labelled "< 0.003%P" and plots low-phosphorus Fe-30Mn-9Al-XSi-0.9C steels at three silicon levels; its legend reads open blue circle = 0.59% Si, open green square = 1.07% Si, open red diamond = 1.56 % Si. (b) is labelled "1% Si" and plots Fe-30Mn-9Al-1Si-0.9C steels at four phosphorus levels; its legend reads open blue circle = 0.001% P, open blue square = 0.006% P, open red diamond = 0.018% P, open red triangle = 0.043% P. In (a) all three curves start at 1 h between roughly 205 and 225 BHN and rise to a plateau near 350 BHN between 50 and 100 h, with the 1.56% Si curve above 0.59% Si during aging while the peak hardnesses are similar. In (b) increasing P both accelerates hardening and raises the peak: 0.043% P attains about 380 BHN near 30 h, whereas 0.001% P peaks near 325 BHN. The paired panels therefore show that both Si and P increase the 530 °C age-hardening response, with phosphorus the stronger effect.

observations.observation: Panel (a) legend lists three silicon levels in a low-phosphorus steel: 0.59% Si (open blue circle), 1.07% Si (open green square) and 1.56 % Si (open red diamond).
Panel (b) legend lists four phosphorus levels in a 1% Si steel: 0.001% P (open blue circle), 0.006% P (open blue square), 0.018% P (open red diamond) and 0.043% P (open red triangle).
Both panels share the same axes: 'Hardness, BHN' from 200 to 400 on the linear y-axis and 'Time in Hours' from 0.1 to 1000 on a logarithmic x-axis.
In panel (a) all three Si curves converge at 1 h between about 205 and 225 BHN and rise to a plateau close to 350 BHN between 50 and 100 h.
In panel (a) the 1.56 % Si (red diamond) curve plots above the 0.59% Si (blue circle) curve at essentially every aging time, while their peak hardnesses near 50-100 h are similar.
In panel (b) the 0.043% P (red triangle) curve is the highest of the four, reaching approximately 380 BHN near 30 h, whereas the 0.001% P (blue circle) curve peaks near 325 BHN.
Every data point in both panels carries vertical error bars, and no numeric hardness values are printed on any data point.
The caption states the figure presents 530 °C age-hardening curves for (a) low-phosphorus Fe-30Mn-9Al-XSi-0.9C steels and (b) Fe-30Mn-9Al-1Si-0.9C steels with between 0.001% and 0.043% P.
The caption states that both Si and P increase hardness during aging.

The citing text states that increasing Si from 0.59% to 1.56% had no effect on solution-treated hardness but increased hardness during aging without significantly increasing the peak hardness (Fig. 2a).
The citing text states phosphorus greatly increases both the hardening rate and the peak hardness during aging of a 1% Si steel (Fig. 2b).
The citing text states that P above 0.006% has a much more pronounced effect on age hardening than Si addition, increasing both hardening rate and maximum aged hardness.
The citing text states that P above 0.006% decreases notch toughness by up to 80% in an aged Fe-30Mn-9Al-1Si-0.9C-0.5Mo steel, a trade-off not visible in this figure.

subfigures.description: Age-hardening scatter plot for low-phosphorus (< 0.003%P) Fe-30Mn-9Al-XSi-0.9C steels; y-axis Hardness, BHN 200-400, log x-axis Time in Hours 0.1-1000; legend: 0.59% Si (blue circle), 1.07% Si (green square), 1.56 % Si (red diamond), all with error bars. Hardness rises from ~205-225 BHN at 1 h to a plateau near 350 BHN at 50-100 h, with 1.56% Si highest during aging but similar peak hardness to 0.59% Si.

Age-hardening scatter plot for 1% Si Fe-30Mn-9Al-1Si-0.9C steels with four phosphorus levels; same axes as (a); legend: 0.001% P (blue circle), 0.006% P (blue square), 0.018% P (red diamond), 0.043% P (red triangle), all with error bars. Higher P shifts the whole curve up and steepens it; 0.043% P peaks near 380 BHN around 30 h while 0.001% P peaks near 325 BHN.
